item.description: Mark Ashton, Ipswich Town's chairman and chief executive, has stated the club's ambition to stabilise in the Premier League and aim for Europe, among a range of topics discussed in an interview with BBC Radio Suffolk. Since taking the role in 2021, Ashton has presided over a period of exceptional success on and off the pitch, including Town twice being promoted to the top flight. In a feature interview, available on BBC Sounds , he discussed the club's transfer strategy, the desire of its investors and their shared vision for the future. Moving on from McKenna The Tractor Boys earned their third promotion in five seasons in May, sealing an immediate return to the top flight after relegation in 2024-25 . Their initial return to the Premier League came off the back of consecutive promotions from League One and the Championship, after years of stagnation since the early 2000s. However, at the end of last season, Kieran McKenna - the manager who guided the club through its period of success - unexpectedly announced he would step down , and was replaced by Gary O'Neil. Ahead of Saturday's trip to fellow promoted side Hull City, they sit 12th in the table. "It's been a little bit of a whirlwind," said Ashton. item.title: Ballon d'Or 2026 voting breakdown: Harry Kane edges out Kylian Mbappe in incredibly tight race as full scores revealed
item.description: FBL-AWARD-BALLON D'OR-2026 - AFP Harry Kane has officially ended England's long wait for a Ballon d'Or winner, but the full voting breakdown reveals just how close the Bayern Munich striker came to missing out. The former Tottenham talisman secured the prestigious Golden Ball in London, edging out his nearest rival, Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe, in a nail-biting finish. A historic and narrow triumph Kane secured the Ballon d'Or by a razor-thin margin of just 28 points. The Bayern Munich striker claimed the coveted award for the first time on Monday, becoming the first English male player to win the prize since Michael Owen in 2001. The glitzy ceremony took place in Kane’s hometown of London, capping off a remarkable year for the Three Lions captain. The final tally highlights a fiercely competitive three-way race. Kane amassed 1,055 points, narrowly defeating Mbappe, who finished a close second with 1,027 points. Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal took third place, trailing significantly with 881 points despite a World Cup-winning campaign with Spain. A tense race to the finish line The polling process was filled with behind-the-scenes drama. France Football editor Vincent Garcia confirmed that the voting window was volatile, with the lead changing hands as the deadline approached . "I was watching the results in real time during the month of the vote," Garcia revealed. "Kylian Mbappe led the race for a long time, but Harry Kane came back into contention, and in the end, it was decided by a very, very small number of points." Following his landmark victory, Kane acknowledged the stiff competition he faced. "Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was really tough this year," he said during his acceptance speech. "Congratulations to all the winners, all the nominees tonight – an impressive showing of what determination and hard work can really achieve, so well done." A year of contrasting fortunes Mbappe’s second-place finish marks his highest-ever Ballon d'Or ranking, surpassing his third-place standing in 2018. The Real Madrid forward dominated scoring charts across La Liga, the Champions League, and the World Cup, yet remains without the Golden Ball. His lack of major club silverware last season likely proved decisive in the final vote. Conversely, Kane’s transition to Germany has been a resounding success. The striker spearheaded Bayern Munich to a domestic league and cup double, cementing their dominance in the Bundesliga. Furthermore, Kane enjoyed crucial head-to-head victories over Mbappe on the biggest stages, notably defeating Real Madrid in the Champions League to reach the semi-finals, and helping England overcome France in the World Cup third-place play-off. item.title: Injured Army veteran represents GB at golf in US
item.description: Steve Dickinson is representing Team GB for the third time [Simpson Cup] An injured Army veteran has been chosen to represent Great Britain in a golf competition against the US. The Simpson Cup is an international tournament for wounded and injured military veterans, taking place from Sunday at Shady Oaks Country Club in Texas. Steve Dickinson, 61, from Peterborough, needed a complete knee replacement for an injury he got after serving with the British Army in the first Gulf War in 1991 . He has been selected for the team for the third consecutive time and said: "Having served my country in uniform, being given the opportunity to represent Great Britain again through sport is something I am immensely proud of." The Simpson Cup has been running since 2012 and raises funds and awareness for the work of the On Course Foundation, which supports the recovery of wounded, injured and sick service personnel and veterans through golf events and opportunities for employment in the golf industry. The Ryder Cup-style tournament "showcases the unique position of golf as one of the few sports where players of all skills and abilities can play together on a level playing field, because of the official golf handicap system", the foundation said. Dickinson plays at Peterborough Milton Golf Club and his handicap is 11.7. He served with the Army Catering Corps between 1981 and 1995. Team GB currently leads the US by seven wins to six in the annual competition. Steve Dickinson celebrated with team members after their last win [Simpson Cup] Speaking about the work of the foundation, Dickinson said: "It helps us get back into civilian life, and the camaraderie, the friendship - it's just about us getting together. "My injury is nothing compared to these guys - some of them are limbless, mine was just playing football in the Army in Cyprus after the Gulf War. "I got injured and five years ago I had a full knee replacement and that's still ongoing and I need it replacing again. So it's never ending — the injury's always there." BBC Sport: Golf The foundation helps with any injury, he said. "It can be physical, it can be mental, but it helps everybody get together... it's such a great, great atmosphere." The tournaments are "full-on banter" with the opponents, "from the minute we get there to the minute we leave", Dickinson said. "We all take the mickey out of each other," he added. "But when we play the Americans, it's a serious competition to be fair; we are serious on the day." Do you have a story suggestion for Peterborough? Contact us below. item.title: “How Many All-Pros Does Tom Brady Have?”: Rob Parker Makes Massive Claim About Lamar Jackson’s NFL Legacy By Comparing Him To 7x SB Winner
item.description: Lamar Jackson © Imagn NFL analyst Rob Parker showered praise on Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson and compared him to seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady. On The Odd Couple Show, Parker highlighted Jackson’s three First-Team All-Pro selections and compared them with Brady, who earned the same number in 23 seasons. “The best quarterback in the NFL is Lamar Jackson,” Parker said. “How many All-Pros does Tom Brady have? Tom Brady had three All-Pros. Three in 23. Lamar has three already in two-thirds less time. He already has three.” Brady also had three Second-Team All-Pro selections. The former Patriots quarterback won three MVP awards, while Jackson has won two. Parker added that Jackson was robbed of the MVP award in 2024 and claimed he had a better season than eventual winner, Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen. “He should have three MVPs,” Parker continued. “The best year he had in the National Football League didn’t give him the MVP. They gave him first-team All-Pro, but they gave Josh Allen the MVP because they felt sorry for him. It went against everything we know in the National Football League. It was terrible.” In that season, Jackson threw for 4,172 yards, 41 touchdowns and four interceptions. Meanwhile, Allen threw for 3,731 yards, 28 touchdowns, and six interceptions. In the voting , Allen received 383 points and 27 first-place votes, while Jackson finished with 362 points and 23 first-place votes. Rob Parker Excuses Lamar Jackson Of Super Bowl-Less Career While Lamar Jackson is considered one of the best quarterbacks in the league, his lack of postseason success takes some of the shine off his career. Tom Brady made 10 Super Bowl appearances and won seven championships. On the other hand, Jackson has zero Super Bowl appearances in eight seasons. However, according to Rob Parker, the Ravens quarterback has been let down by his teammates. “Zay Flowers, a fumble. Mark Andrews can’t catch a two-point conversion to tie the game in Buffalo. It’s happened over and over again,” Parker said. “Last year, to get into the playoffs and to win the division, guess what happened? Lamar drove the team down the field in Pittsburgh, and the kicker missed a field goal.” Jackson has missed three straight games due to a high ankle sprain sustained in Week 4, but is expected to return when the Ravens face the Bills on Sunday. item.title: WWE succession plan emerges as Shawn Michaels and AJ Styles eye new roles
item.description: Photo by MICHAEL TRAN/AFP via Getty Images WWE Hall of Famers Shawn Michaels and AJ Styles are reportedly in line for major backstage promotions as the company prepares for a significant change in its creative leadership. Bruce Prichard, WWE’s Executive Director of Creative Writing and Talent, is expected to retire after WrestleMania 43, although he could remain involved with the company as a consultant. Michaels is reportedly being lined up to replace Prichard in 2027, while Styles could take on a more hands-on role with WWE’s developmental brand, NXT. Shawn Michaels could replace Bruce Prichard as AJ Styles takes on NXT role According to reports from PWInsider , Michaels is expected to move into Prichard’s position, with preparations for the transition already expected to begin in the coming months. The former WWE champion has led NXT since 2021, when Paul ‘Triple H’ Levesque underwent a cardiac procedure. Michaels was subsequently promoted to Senior Vice President of Talent Development and Creative. His experience with developing young wrestlers makes him a natural candidate for a more prominent position within WWE’s creative structure. Michaels also shares a longstanding friendship with Triple H, which could prove valuable as the pair continue shaping the company’s future. However, his potential promotion would leave a significant opening at NXT, with AJ Styles reportedly emerging as a candidate to take on greater responsibilities. According to False Finish, WWE officials expect Styles to become more involved with the developmental brand following Michaels’ departure from the role. Styles has previously expressed a desire to help prepare the next generation of WWE superstars, particularly after stepping away from in-ring competition. Triple H discussed the former champion’s plans during an appearance on Cody Rhodes’ podcast, explaining that Styles had explored several backstage positions before identifying the area that suited him best. “He really likes is getting to these young kids, spotting talent, and trying to help fan the flames of that little spark and turn it into something more, the developmental side,” Triple H said. Styles’ interest in mentoring young wrestlers could make him a strong fit for NXT, where emerging talent is prepared for the main roster. The Phenomenal One brings plenty of experience to the role, having won both WWE and TNA World Championships and becoming one of just 22 Grand Slam champions in WWE history. Styles was also inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame during WrestleMania 42 week. With Prichard’s expected retirement approaching, WWE could soon have two familiar names taking on new responsibilities behind the scenes. item.title: Teen football photographer 'living the dream'
item.description: Tiego Greno has progressed from photographing lower league matches to Premier League games [Tiego Greno] From taking photos of grassroots football matches up to Champions League games - all by the age of 18 - Tiego Greno says he is "living the dream". The teenager from Chelmsford started taking photos of lower league football in 2023, before becoming Chelmsford City's club photographer for the 2025-26 season. Now he has started taking photos of Premier League and European matches, including Arsenal's recent away fixture against Bayern Munich. "I just want to be everywhere, every single day if it's possible," he told the BBC. Greno started work with a photography agency aged 17 which was something he says came with challenges, given his age. "Many of these stadiums don't allow anyone under 18 to work in those environments, so I had to be restricted," he told BBC Essex's James Patient. Still only 18, Greno's photography has taken him to stadiums including Real Madrid's Bernabeu [Tiego Greno] But his work began to speak for itself. Just three days after his 18th birthday, he won the sports category at the East Anglian Photography Awards, with his photo of Southend United players crestfallen as their opponents Oldham Athletic celebrated promotion back to the Football League at Wembley Stadium in June 2025. "I think that picture really summarised what can happen in the sport - you could be winning for the entire game and then in the last minute it all turns around," he said. Greno says he is grateful to his family for being able to afford his camera equipment, especially his father and fellow photographer Antonio. "Without him, probably I wouldn't be where I am right now," he said. Antonio said it was "impossible not to be proud" of his son. "For me, this journey has been… more than photography, it's been about watching my son discovering what he loves and, most importantly, having the courage to follow," he told the BBC. His son said: "I'm already living the dream. It's just keeping it really consistent and if I can do it every day, perfect." Do you have a story suggestion for Essex? Contact us below. item.description: Mission Viejo High players and coaches pose for a photo after winning the Alpha League title on Friday night at San Juan Hills (Caleb Otte / For The Times) Scoring 44 points in a league championship decider is usually enough to secure victory — but not against Mission Viejo. The Diablos beat San Juan Hills 54-44 in an epic Orange County shootout to secure its third consecutive Alpha League crown, buoyed by a bevy of explosive plays. It started in the first quarter as senior running back Carson Vandermade, who returned after missing the last two games, scored two touchdowns. He finished the game with 121 yards, including a big 52-yard run down the sideline, and three touchdowns but did not return for the fourth quarter. His counterpart, senior Jack Junker, gained 132 yards, including a 28-yarder, and two touchdowns as the Diablos’ rushing attack dominated. Every time Vandermade and Junker took handoffs, there was a gift waiting. The offensive line — which has four players either committed to or with offers to Division I colleges — opened up huge running lanes. Junior center Max Davidson attributed the group’s success to a deep camaraderie and hard work. “It comes down to all the time that we put in together,” he said. “It comes down to the chemistry that we have between the five of us up front. We work together really well and that shows in all our games.” Mission Viejo High center Max Davidson is all smiles after the Diablos won the Alpha League title with a 54-44 victory over San Juan Hills on Friday night. In an era of basketball where consistency from three-point range is preached as paramount, the Detroit Pistons are winning in their own way. Their tough defense and efficiency inside the paint has defined their identity this season," SI's Aidan Chacon wrote. Adding a shooter will undoubtedly be one of the Pistons' priorities ahead of the trade deadline. CBS Sports' Sam Quinn believes they should pursue a trade for NBA champion Michael Porter Jr. “Get ready to hear a lot about the Detroit Pistons today, folks. A team that needs offense and controls all of its own picks is always going to feature prominently in deadline speculation, and Porter is the first of many candidates who will come up for them here,” Quinn wrote. Porter would be a great addition because he offers exactly what the team needs as a shooter while also bringing NBA Finals experience. He could become an important presence in Detroit's locker room as well. Porter is currently playing on a $179 million contract with the Brooklyn Nets and is coming off a strong campaign last season. If the Pistons want to add a proven scorer, Porter would certainly be a good option. item.description: “We’re still working”: Eva Olid promises more from her free-flowing Man United Women team Manchester United Women manager Eva Olid has spoken to the media ahead of her side’s match against Everton Women this afternoon. Evolution The first topic she addressed was how her team has evolved since the start of the season, explaining, “yeah, especially in terms of the confidence the team now have in possession and out of possession. We look like a totally different team, but, as I say, we’re still the same team. The only difference is that we’ve now had more weeks working together, and we can feel that we understand each other better.” She also stated that while her side can enjoy their current form, they must be prepared for changes, explaining, “we’re in a good moment, but we know how football works. During a season, you have ups and downs, and you always need to be ready for when things go well and when they don’t. You need to stay together and solve situations as a team. At the beginning of the season, we had two bad performances, but we were able to work together to understand what was happening and how we could improve.” The derby last weekend Reflecting on the 1-1 draw with Manchester City last weekend, Olid explained that the crowd numbers were similar to what she experienced in Heart of Midlothian matches against Hibernian, but overall, “we really enjoyed it. We were speaking with the staff about how much we enjoyed Sunday because the fans were with us. We could hear them, and these are the nights we are involved in football for. We enjoyed everything about it: the way the team played, the fans and the intensity of the game. These kinds of matches make us happy.” Spanish talent moving to club Olid was then asked about how she, her coaches, and player Andrea Medina are adapting to life at the club. "It will never go back to how it was," he said. "I am still playing with pain. But these are the risks you take for the national team, I’d do it again."
